chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the command is in the eldest, so long as there is no disability in him.

key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: the command or authority, here referring to the matter of Imamate
key_terms.الْكَبِيرِ: the eldest or senior one among those under consideration
key_terms.عَاهَةٌ: a disabling defect, impairment, or incapacitating condition
key_terms.قَالَ: he said, introducing the statement of the Imam عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: According to this hadith, when does the command of Imamate remain with the eldest?
ai.summary: This hadith states a principle regarding the succession of the divine authority, indicating that it belongs to the eldest among the eligible descendants unless there is an incapacitating defect in him. In Shia theological context, it relates to the order and designation of the Imam and the conditions relevant to religious authority.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The command (Imamate) is in the eldest, for as long as there does not happen to be a inability (Caused by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, i.e., death) for him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Yahya al-Wasiti from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“The leadership is with being the elder as long as he is free of defects.”
